2075f496799c: feat(flights): **your Vector Vario data shows up even when your flight app wrote the file, and heart rate gets its own tab.** If a navigation app paired with your Vector Vario over Bluetooth records the flight, We-Fly now reads the Vector's airspeed, pitch and roll, load factor, netto, temperature, humidity and measured wind from that file too: the **Vector Vario** tab appears and the **Wind** tab switches to the measured wind, exactly as for a file from the Vector itself. If your app also records your heart rate from a chest strap, a new **Heart rate** tab shows your average, peak and lowest pulse, your pulse from takeoff to landing over your altitude, the time spent in each heart-rate band and how it changed between thermalling and gliding. Heart rate is health data, so only you see that tab: We-Fly reads it from your file when you open it and stores none of it, and when someone you share the flight with, or a pilot browsing the community, downloads its file, they get it without your heart rate. In the **Logbook**, two new columns (hidden by default, under **Columns**) mark the flights with **Vector Vario** data and with **Heart rate**, and you can sort by them.
b4bba26dac92: feat(xc-planner): **save your briefing's airspace file and load it into your instrument.** At the end of the **XC planner**, the **Airspace file** section now has **Save to my account** next to the download: give the file a name, pick OpenAir **v2.1** or **v1**, and it is kept for 30 days under **Saved files**, where you can download or delete it. Apps and instruments you connected to your account with the airspace permission can fetch these files through the We-Fly API, so your planned airspace can reach the cockpit without copying a file by hand. After 30 days the file is deleted automatically.
5d346b75be92: docs(blog): **We-Fly enters beta, and you can help translate it.** A new blog post explains what the beta means on the road to 1.0, walks through everything that now speaks French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish, and shows step by step how to suggest a better wording, either through **Contact** or by editing the public translations on GitHub.
592352c06634: feat(email): **follow We-Fly on YouTube, Facebook and Instagram from any email.** Every email We-Fly sends now ends with links to our YouTube channel, Facebook page and Instagram account, in your language, so you can catch the video tours, news and flying pictures in one tap.
282313d1711c: feat(i18n): **the help articles in your language.** All 28 help articles, from uploading and syncing your instrument to the thermal, glide, G-force and statistics guides, now read in French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish, with the buttons and menus named exactly as you see them in the app. Search engines list each article in every language. The privacy policy, terms of service and data retention policy are translated too; the English text remains the one that applies, and those pages say so.
30c151cc0579: feat(i18n): **emails in your language.** Every email We-Fly sends you now arrives in the language you picked: account and password emails, flight review requests and annotations, tips to get started, the community survey invitation, the messages your safety contacts get when you take off, land or raise an alert, and the data retention notices. Your safety contacts receive them in your language too. Dates are written the way your language writes them.
efa895984e44: feat(i18n): **release notes in your language.** The **What's New** window and the release history on the **About** page now speak French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish, from version 1.0.0-alpha.1 on, with section titles and dates written the way your language writes them. A note that is not translated yet simply shows in English, and older releases stay in English with a short note saying so. The About page can now be found by search engines in every language.
ffd2e9ec6954: feat(i18n): **the XC planner in your language.** The whole **XC planner** now speaks French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish: route design, the competition task designer with its checks and tips, airspaces and the vertical cut, NOTAMs, the briefing with its weather, waypoint collections and the 3D review. Distances, heights and speeds in the route summary, the task checks, the briefing, the vertical cut and the 3D review now follow your unit settings, and the planner has its own page in each language, so pilots searching in their language can find it. A shared route or task shows its preview in the reader's language.
0fee577ce21b: feat(i18n): **the community, takeoffs and shared pages in your language.** The **Community** hub, feeds, pilots, leaderboard, stats, clubs, challenges and season recap, the **Takeoffs** list and every takeoff page (with its flyability verdict), **Place to be**, the flight search map, **Wings**, live tracking, the community survey, the map controls and the public pages you share (flights, pilots, replays, clubs, recaps) now speak French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish. Search engines can now find each takeoff page and shared page in every language.
c6f159ea8fdc: feat(i18n): **your logbook, every flight and your cockpit in your language.** The **Logbook** with its filters and bulk actions, the whole flight page (summary, phases, thermals, wind, speed, vario, G-force, weather, competition task, Vector Vario, notes, airspace files), the 2D and 3D replay, the same-day comparison, your season recap and the **Cockpit** statistics now speak French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish. Thermal coaching tips are written for your language and your units, country names follow your language, and compass points use your local letters (O for west in French, Italian and Spanish).
729b04b59e00: feat(i18n): **sign in, your profile and uploads in your language.** Signing in, creating an account, resetting your password, the privacy consent, your **Profile** with all its settings, your badges on **Success** and the **Upload** page now speak French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish, including the error messages. You can also pick your language from the new **Language** row in your display settings. Badge names follow your language too, and dates, weekdays and months are written the way your language writes them.
6e93f594d363: feat(i18n): **the documentation speaks your language.** The **Docs** hub, search, categories, the **About**, **Contact** and **References** pages are now translated into French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish. Help articles show up in your language as soon as their translation is published; until then you read the English version with a short note saying so, and links between articles keep you in your language. Translated legal pages remind you that the English text is the one that applies, and every translated article has a link to suggest a better wording.
f8d2fe7bb759: feat(i18n): **We-Fly now speaks French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish.** Pick your language from the new **Language** entry in your avatar menu (or the globe on the public pages) and We-Fly remembers it on every device you sign in on. The navigation, menus and home page are translated first; the rest of the app follows release by release, and anything not translated yet simply stays in English. Translations use the words pilots really say at takeoff, and you can suggest better ones: everything lives in the public [we-fly-translations](https://github.com/Djang0/we-fly-translations) project. English links keep working exactly as before.
5fbc1726c5bd: feat(wings): **see how your glide compares with other pilots on the same wing.** Under a wing's **Glide performance (estimate)** on the **Wings** page, open **Compare with other pilots on this wing** to put your trim and on-bar airspeed, sink and glide ratio next to the same estimate built from other pilots' public flights on that wing, on one chart and in one table, with a plain summary such as "at trim you fly 2 km/h faster than the others". Pilots type the wing name into their instrument, so you choose which spellings count as your wing with the same picker as the community comparison, starting from the likely matches of your own wing name. Your own flights are never counted in the other pilots' figures, and those figures only appear once at least 3 other pilots flew the wing. Your choice stays in the link.
2d873ab72d00: feat(wings): **give a wing its own colour in the logbook.** On the **Wings** page, the new round button next to the rename pencil lets you pick a colour for a wing (or none). Every logbook flight on that wing then gets a thin coloured edge on its left side, so a season on several wings, or a tandem wing next to your solo one, is easy to tell apart at a glance. Nothing else in the row changes, and wings without a colour look exactly as before. The colour follows the exact wing name: rename a wing and it keeps its colour; merge it into a wing that already has one and that colour stays.
feb9686aad8d: feat(flights): **see who shared your thermals, and how you climbed against them.** The same-day comparison has a new **Thermals** tab listing every climb where another pilot was in the same thermal as you: circling within 350 m of you, through at least 150 m of the same heights, and passing those heights within three minutes of you. Each climb is compared only over the heights you both climbed through, so staying for the weak top of a thermal never counts against anyone, and the tab shows the best rate anyone reached there next to yours ("3.7 m/s by Emile, you 2.1 m/s, 56%"), plus how far ahead or behind each pilot was, their wing and their turns. Pick a climb and the replay jumps to it while the map zooms in on everyone's core and the combined core of the thermal. The comparison also counts your shared thermals at the top, and **3D** opens the climb in a 3D view with every pilot in it: each climb in the pilot's colour (or coloured by climb rate), the combined core of the thermal next to each pilot's own, rings at the heights you shared, and one clock that replays everyone together with their live climb rate. Wings sink at different rates, so compare like with like.
403d5ed336df: feat(leagues): **send your flights to the CFD and DHV-XC from We-Fly.** Add your FFVL or DHV-XC login once under **Profile → Connected services → Online leagues**, then pick **Send to league** in any flight's menu, or switch on **Send new flights automatically** so every upload goes straight on to your league. We-Fly checks the login before saving it and keeps the password encrypted. For the CFD, We-Fly creates the draft declaration and gives you the link: open it to add your turnpoints and airspace info, then send it, as the CFD requires. The menu shows what each league answered (sent, already there, login refused) so you know where every flight stands. If a league stops accepting your login (you changed the password there), automatic sending pauses and your profile tells you to update it, instead of We-Fly retrying a wrong password on every upload.
8378f7d60181: feat(wings): **see how your wing really glides.** Expand a wing on the **Wings** page and a new **Glide performance (estimate)** section shows its speed through the air, sink rate and still-air glide ratio, at trim and on bar, worked out from your own straight glides. We remove the wind measured in your thermals from your GPS speed, keep only steady 30-second glide stretches, and show medians so a single glide through rising or sinking air can't swing the result. A speed-vs-sink chart shows every glide as a dot, and **How is this calculated?** explains each number in plain words. It's an estimate to set beside the manufacturer's figures, not a certified polar. It appears once a wing has straight glides from 10 flights, with a confidence level that grows as you log more.
cb45be827180: feat(community): **compare any wings across the whole community.** The **Wings** tab of the community leaderboard now has its own **Compare wings** panel, with the same glide chart and side-by-side table, built from every pilot's flights. Because each pilot types the wing name into their instrument, one wing turns up as "Rush 6", "OZONE Rush6" or "Ozone Rush 6", so you decide what counts as a wing: add one from the search or the compare button on any row, then tick every spelling that belongs to it (or "Select all" on the likely matches or your search results), even rare ones with a single flight, apply them in one go, and give it your own name. The comparison lives in the link, so you can send it to your club. Only public flights count, and a wing flown by fewer than 3 pilots shows its counts but no figures, so nobody can read one pilot's flights through it.
305edbc1e9c0: feat(wings): **compare your wings side by side.** Below the list on the **Wings** page, pick two to four wings to compare (the two you fly most are compared until you choose). Their glide estimates share one speed-vs-sink chart, each wing in its own colour with its trim and on-bar figures joined by a line, and a table lines up trim and accelerated airspeed, sink and glide next to climb rate, XC scores, highest altitude and airtime, with the best value in each row marked. Your choice stays in the link, so you can bookmark or share the comparison. While a wing's older flights are still being processed, its glide panel now says so instead of asking you for more flights.
f303e7492443: feat(cockpit): **see how your flying changes over time.** A new **Trends** view in the Cockpit draws your flights on a real timeline, by day, week, month or year, over the last 30 days, the last 12 months, this year or everything. Choose air time, number of flights, average distance, average air time or average speed (scored distance over air time), and split it by glider to see when you switched wings and what it changed. Click a column, or a glider's part of it, and the logbook opens on exactly those flights; **Show all flights** brings back the full list without touching your saved filters. A table view lists every period with all five numbers.
9bd28d62e18f: feat(admin): **a System tab in the admin menu.** Server health and Disk cleanup now sit under their own **System** tab, next to Developer, instead of being reachable only from links on the admin dashboard.
fc2594ecc608: feat(flights): **measure any stretch of your flight.** On the flight map, drag across the altitude, vario, speed or G-force chart and a bar above the map shows that stretch: start and end time, duration, distance flown, average speed along your track and straight-line speed from start to end (the one that tells you how much circling cost you), height gained or lost, average vario and, on a glide, the glide ratio. The map zooms to that stretch and outlines it in orange, with a dot where it starts and ends, without hiding the speed or vario colours. The selection stays when you switch charts, lives in the link so you can share "look at this glide", and the cross clears it. Distances use the full-resolution track with GPS glitches filtered out, so they match the rest of the page.
378a2bce3b78: feat(admin): **a server health page for admins, so incidents get caught before pilots notice.** A new **Server** tile on the admin dashboard and an **System → Server health** page check the host (CPU load, memory, swap, pending reboot and security updates), the disks behind IGC files, profile pictures, SRTM tiles and logs (space, inodes, write permission), the PM2 workers (online, memory against the restart limit, recent restarts), Apache's worker pool, the public site round-trip, the TLS certificate's days left, and MongoDB and Redis latency. Each problem comes with the first thing to try. Everything runs as the regular, non-root app user.
d740da7b75cc: feat(admin): **server health now watches the MongoDB log.** A new **MongoDB log size** check on the Server health page adds up the database log and its old rotated copies, turning amber at 1 GB and red at 5 GB, so a log that is never rotated is caught long before it fills the disk and stops uploads. When it trips, the page says how to set up log rotation.
bee7d9b88824: feat(admin): **free disk space in an emergency without losing anything that matters.** A new **Disk cleanup** page, linked from Server health and the admin dashboard, scans the server for files We-Fly can rebuild: track caches, G-force and Vector Vario data, terrain tiles, plus leftovers such as abandoned data exports and duplicate legacy files. Admins choose what to clear, how much space to win back, and a window of recently viewed flights that stays untouched. The least recently used files go first. Your original IGC files are never touched, and every cleanup is logged with who ran it and how much it freed.
d75b80187bcf: feat(admin): **answer every survey participant personally.** The community survey admin page has a new **Participations** view listing every response grouped by pilot (account-linked pilots together, anonymous answers one by one). Each participation can be marked as processed, so the team knows who has been answered, and **Copy AI prompt** puts a ready-made prompt on the clipboard that asks an AI assistant to draft a friendly, professional reply, with short clarification questions wherever an answer is unclear.
cf105216ea0f: feat(email): **choose whether We-Fly sends you tips.** A new **Emails** entry in your profile has a **Tips to get started** switch, and every tip email now carries a one-click unsubscribe link that Gmail and Apple Mail also show as their own Unsubscribe button. The privacy policy now explains these tips and how to turn them off.
98093f5a5158: docs(help): **help articles that match the app again.** Twenty-two help articles were checked against today's screens and corrected: button and menu names, the Cockpit views, the thermal tab, how the thermal score is calculated (with fresh worked examples), how thermals are detected (the old settings page no longer exists, so that article now explains what the detection does), the leaderboard columns, filters, FAI validation and how to get a copy of your data. The privacy policy now lists every cookie We-Fly sets, including the language ones, and the profile's export row says the archive contains a JSON copy of your data, not a CSV.
5666394f2444: perf(i18n): **pages load less text.** Each page now sends your browser only the interface text it actually shows, instead of every translation in the app. The Docs pages carry about 60% less, and pages such as your profile about 85% less, which helps most on slow mobile connections at the foot of a hill.
038b886f20a0: fix(flights): **your original IGC files are never changed any more.** Correcting a flight's wing or date, renaming a wing, or importing from Logfly with a different wing name used to rewrite the stored IGC file to match. Now the correction is saved in your logbook only, and the file stays exactly as your instrument recorded it, so a downloaded IGC is always the genuine one you would submit to a league or a competition. Uploading the same flight again keeps the file already stored.
f7f66b9d0dea: feat(flights): **a better-looking, easier-to-read 3D view of your thermals.** The single-thermal 3D view and the new shared-thermal view now use We-Fly's own colours on a warm background (deep charcoal in dark mode), with distance fog for depth. The thermal is a soft glowing column that widens and narrows with your turns, with its core as a bright line and bubbles rising at the pace of the climb. Your track is solid where the replay has been and faint ahead, its shadow sits on the ground grid, a dashed line drops from you to the ground, and an altitude scale stands beside the climb, so height and position read at a glance. Climb-rate colours match the 2D thermal map. The view eases in when it opens, unless you have asked your device for reduced motion.
95182e0cce8e: feat(admin): **server health follows the move from Apache to nginx.** The web server check on the Server health page now reads nginx's status page and flags dropped connections, with requests per second and open connections alongside. It still recognises Apache, so nothing goes dark while the server switches over. The public round-trip and certificate checks are unchanged.
80701882b772: feat(flights): **the Wind tab uses your Vector Vario's measured wind when it has one.** On flights logged with a Vector Vario, wind direction, speed, altitude bands and the speed × altitude heatmap now come from the instrument's second-by-second wind readings instead of being estimated from thermal drift, so you also get wind for glides and flights with few thermals. A **Measured by Vector Vario** badge next to the confidence pill tells you which source you are looking at. Flights from other instruments keep the thermal-drift estimate as before.
f3e6e4a8fa32: feat(email): **a more useful welcome reminder when your logbook is still empty.** The reminder now leads with the fastest route for XCTrack and Air³ pilots: set up FolderSync once, with your server address and username already filled in, and every flight lands in We-Fly on its own. It also lists the other ways in: moving over from XContest, Syride, SeeYou or Logfly, Flyskyhy, Google Drive, or a plain upload. It now arrives exactly a week after you sign up, and reads well on a phone.
578dbf97cd0a: fix(xc-planner): **the Select button is back in the airspace list.** When you click the map where several airspaces stack up, a long airspace name (such as "LOWER CTA BRUSSELS MINUS LUXEMBOURG…") pushed **Select**, **Show** and the info button off the edge of the window, so you could not add the airspace to your briefing. Long names are now shortened, the buttons always stay in view, and on a phone they sit on their own line under the name.
9200e97424cb: fix(upload): **a log recorded without flying now gets a clear answer.** Uploading a track that never left the ground, such as an instrument test at home, used to fail with "Server error, try again later", which no retry could fix. We-Fly now tells you straight away that the file has no usable GPS points.
f64cc7252ea0: fix(observability): **no more error reports when your connection drops in Firefox.** A page that stopped loading because the network dropped ("Error in input stream" in Firefox) is no longer reported to us as a We-Fly bug, the same as in the other browsers.
0124f00972b1: fix(observability): **fewer false alarms from your browser.** Errors thrown by scripts that the browser itself adds to a page, such as the crypto wallet built into Brave or the in-app browser of Facebook and Instagram on Android, are no longer reported as We-Fly errors. Nothing changes for you, but the real problems you run into reach us faster.
f47d2702e0a9: fix(i18n): **the French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish pages open again.** If you had picked a language, opening a page in it (for example we-fly.cloud/fr) ended with "too many redirects" instead of the page. Every translated public page now loads normally.
82653c73519f: fix(home): **signed in, the home page takes you straight to your logbook.** The big button on the home page still offered to sign you in with a passkey when you were already signed in. It now reads "Go to your logbook" and opens your flights.
1e889d57e616: fix(i18n): **the controls above a flight, the docs and the planner speak your language in full.** The share button and the hints on the flight page's tab bar, and the matching controls above the docs and the XC planner, could fall back to raw text codes because that bar did not receive the page's translations. They now read in your language like the rest of the page.
e6adf9f6e2c6: chore(deps): **steadier forms and screens under the hood.** A newer code checker flagged screens that updated themselves in a roundabout way. Dialogs (edit name, takeoff, airspace, annotation, flight date) now reset cleanly each time they open, editing a takeoff no longer risks wiping what you typed when the page refreshes in the background, and the sign-in, upload, thermal, replay and planner screens do less redundant re-rendering.
4817a398aad5: fix(i18n): **clock times and file sizes in your language.** The time readouts on the altitude, speed and climb charts, the segment stats and the map now follow your language while staying on a 24-hour clock, and the video export writes file sizes the way your language does (4,3 Mo in French). A stricter check now stops new English text from slipping into the app.
1efbe02163ca: fix(i18n): **flight types, dates and calendars follow your language.** The flight type in your logbook, on the flight page and in its summary now reads in your language instead of English or a title-cased guess. Calendars show months and weekdays in your language, date ranges and the time zone in the 3D replay and video export are written your way, the video export shows altitude in your own unit, and the flight page title, link previews and the season recap heading are translated.
7a8bccf98ce1: fix(i18n): **airspace and NOTAM labels follow your language.** Airspace types and classes (Restricted, Danger, Prohibited, Class D), the type and activity in the airspace details, NOTAM subjects such as "Danger area" or "Parachute jumping", NOTAM zone names in the 3D review, the airspace alert in the 3D replay and the START and GOAL pills of the 3D planner review no longer fall back to English. Airspace names from the map data stay as published.
51a63f6466a3: fix(i18n): **community labels no longer slip back into English.** The weekday names and flight types on the community stats charts, the most common type, the records and leaderboards, the following feed, clubs, challenges, Place to be, instrument statistics, the flight search map and the season recap now show their weekday, flight type and placeholder names (Anonymous, Unknown takeoff, Other) in your language instead of English.
16e88c1baccf: fix(i18n): **errors in the planner, the uploads and your profile now speak your language.** Messages that came back from the server in English now follow the language you picked: why an IGC file was refused (upload and same-day comparison), why a task file, code or XContest cloud code could not be imported, saving, publishing and deleting routes, tasks and waypoint collections in the XC planner (including the prompt to sign in), Logfly import problems, and the profile sharing link. A takeoff without a name in your shared flights and replays is also translated.
000eeac0d6cb: fix(i18n): **error messages and consent pages follow your language.** Toasts about shared flight and replay links, airspace files, review requests, email preferences and failed requests, the OAuth authorization and device pages with their permission lists, and the confirm or remove page that safety contacts open from an email, were showing English whatever language you picked. They now speak yours.
89ad4f09cc7f: fix(profile): **flight types on your profile speak your language.** The flights-by-type breakdown on your profile, your statistics and pilot profiles showed the scorer's English names whatever language you picked. They are now translated, like everywhere else. Flights the scorer could not classify are counted as Free Flight in those breakdowns and in your data export, instead of a technical free_flight label.
a08605631162: fix(export): **the total distance in your data export is right.** The README inside the archive you download from your profile showed your total distance in kilometres, but the number was really in metres, so 1,250 km read as 1,250,000 km. It now shows real kilometres, and a new section lists the unit of every number in the JSON file (metres for the track distance, kilometres for the scored distance, seconds for durations).
5a8d4e060cc9: fix(i18n): **the last English corners now follow your language.** The notifications menu, the light and dark mode switch, the share menu, the error page, the rate-limit notice, close buttons and date pickers, the Pioneer badge, the 3D thermal legend, the takeoff edit, delete and rename dialogs, the page that explains how to **move your flights to We-Fly**, and the screen where you let an app or a flight instrument access your account were still in English. They are now ready for French, German, Dutch, Italian and Spanish.
b6e56c2816b4: fix(cockpit): **the Median G-factor card really shows a median.** It showed the single highest value among your filtered flights, so one rough day set the number for the whole season. It is now the median across those flights, worked out the same way as the circling-time and circle-radius cards beside it, and written with your language's decimal separator.
840cdfdd3976: fix(takeoffs): **flight types on takeoff pages keep igc-xc-score's names.** The flight type shown in a takeoff's statistics and recent flights is now exactly the one the scorer gives (Free Flight, Free Triangle, FAI Triangle, Closed Free Triangle, Closed FAI Triangle), translated into your language, each with its own colour dot. A leftover label that called flat triangles "Closed FAI" could never match the stored type and is gone.
2efc4d611e15: fix(i18n): **numbers are written the way your language writes them.** Distances, speeds, climb rates, altitudes, scores and percentages now use your language's decimal comma and thousands separator (7,8 km and 1 850 m in French, 1.850 m in German) everywhere in the app, while still following your unit settings. English stays exactly as before. Dates and counts no longer depend on your browser's settings, which could make some pages flicker as they loaded.
d45ca2ac57c2: fix(badges): **every badge you earn now shows up in your notifications and the badge catalog.** When the team adjusts a badge's steps (say, a Thermal Power badge at 4 m/s instead of the default tiers), badges earned on those steps went missing from the notification bell, the catalog listed the default steps instead of the ones you can actually earn, and the community season recap left them out of its badge counts. All three now follow the steps in force.
8407a009850b: fix(flights): **re-analysing your flights no longer loses your low saves and bar use, or turns a tow into a thermal.** When We-Fly re-runs its flight analysis after an improvement, towed and powered launches keep the launch climb out of your thermals, the driving at either end of a track is trimmed as on upload, and the low saves and speed-bar figures are kept instead of coming back empty. Re-analysed flights now match a fresh upload.
c4dbedc3cb15: fix(layout): **long pages no longer slide the whole app up while you scroll.** On long pages such as an expanded wing on the **Wings** page, scrolling could move the entire app, top bar included, up out of the window and leave an empty band at the bottom. Hidden screen-reader labels were stretching the page behind the app; they now stay inside it, so only the content scrolls and the top bar stays put.
c90a0f4c14e2: fix(observability): **errors from Brave and Firefox on iPhone no longer count as We-Fly bugs.** Those browsers add their own helper scripts to every page, and when one of them trips up, it used to be reported as if We-Fly had crashed. Those reports are now ignored, so real problems stand out in our error tracking.
7b5c2d744fdb: fix(maps): **no more crash when you leave a map right after zooming.** Switching base layer or leaving a page with a vector map (such as the Community map) during the short settle after a zoom no longer throws an error.
c222e9a3633a: fix(nav): **one browser's quirk can no longer take down every page.** The About dialog's release notes now load only when you open it, so a browser that cannot run that part (seen on Chrome 138) loses the About dialog instead of the whole app, and every page starts with less code to load.
3dfbb967f2a1: fix(xc-planner): **Skyways seasons load again.** Picking Spring, Summer or Autumn asked thermal.kk7.ch for datasets it does not have, so the overlay went blank. The seasons now use kk7's own names, Winter joins the list, and a season saved in your browser under the old names falls back to All year instead of a blank map.
d1ab3810e4e4: fix(admin): **server health says why Apache workers are not monitored when the status page is redirected.** If Apache answers the local status probe with a redirect (typically the HTTP→HTTPS rule on the port-80 site), the check now names the redirect and where it points, instead of suggesting to enable `mod_status` again, and the server-health doc gives the small Apache site that fixes it.
c8156bc5d2e2: fix(xc-planner): **the Skyways Layer, Season and Time pickers open again.** In the XC planner's Map layers panel (and the Layers menu on flight maps), these lists were opening behind the panel, so clicking them seemed to do nothing. They now open on top.
bc6d79671025: fix(api): **highest and lowest altitude are back in flight data.** The community wing statistics averaged every wing's highest altitude as 0 m, and `GET /api/v1/flights/{id}` sent partner apps neither the highest nor the lowest altitude of a flight, because both read a field name the flights are not stored under. Both now read the stored figures.
9b7b40236ac8: fix(auth): **stay signed in between flying days.** We-Fly used to sign you out after 24 hours without opening the app, so most pilots had to log in again on every visit. You now stay signed in for 30 days of inactivity (a full re-login is asked every 90 days), and a brief database hiccup no longer signs everyone out. Deleting your account or resetting your password still ends every session immediately.
cbd71d32d3dc: fix(auth): **resetting your password now signs out every other device for good.** An old copy of your session, say on a phone you lost, could get itself signed back in after a password reset, and could even add another Google, Facebook or GitHub login to your account. Now a reset or an account deletion ends every other session at its next request, and a social login only joins your account when it uses your account's email. Admins who impersonate a pilot are signed out too if their own sessions are revoked or their admin role is removed.
eaa2f723ff6c: docs(privacy): **the Data Retention Policy and the Privacy Policy now say how long you really stay signed in.** The retention policy still said sessions end after 7 days, and the privacy policy only called the sign-in cookie "session-based". Both now give the real rules: 30 days after your last visit, 90 days at most, and straight away when you sign out, reset your password or delete your account.
0c38ca9fe94f: fix(deps): **math in the guides now renders with the patched KaTeX.** The math plugins carried their own outdated copy of KaTeX with a known security flaw; they now share the app's up-to-date one, which also keeps the formulas' HTML and styles from the same version. Two build tools were updated to their patched releases too.
df2289582b18: fix(admin): **the MongoDB log size check explains why it shows n/a.** On the server the MongoDB log folder is closed to the app user, so the check could not read it and only said n/a. Its hint now names the cause and the one-line fix (`sudo chmod 0755 /var/log/mongodb`, which reveals file names and sizes only, never the log contents), and the setup guide says the same.
f961bd53bd9d: fix(flights): **downloading the IGC file from a flight's Summary tab no longer fires failed requests in the background.** The file name link tried to preload the download as if it were a page, which the server refused. It is now a plain download link. We also silenced a chart sizing warning removed leftover debug messages from the upload page, and stopped every page from preloading the public site footer's styles it never uses, so the browser console stays clean when something real needs looking at.
aa25b1168419: fix(flights): **the map marker follows the altitude chart inside a zoomed stretch.** After selecting part of your flight, hovering the altitude chart under the map put the pilot marker (and the readout above the chart) near takeoff instead of at the moment under your cursor. It now lands on the right spot of the stretch you are looking at.
90baa4a4c65b: fix(flights): **your logbook shows your hours and distance again.** The line above your flights reads, for example, "25 of 96 flights · 142h 30m · 3210 km". The hours and kilometres add up every flight that matches your filters, not only the ones loaded on screen, so they are right without scrolling to the bottom. Change a filter and they follow.
9bb144de9287: fix(flights): **old flights no longer lose their G-force chart, sketch, preview image or recap trace when a cached track file is missing.** These now rebuild the track from your original IGC file on the spot, like the flight map already did. The JSON track download recovers the same way.
3cb7d1603351: fix(email): **the welcome reminder for pilots with an empty logbook actually goes out now.** A date mix-up meant nobody ever qualified for it. It also no longer gets lost on a hiccup. If our mail provider refuses the message, the reminder is now tried again on the next run instead of being silently dropped, and every failure is reported to our error monitoring without your email address in the logs.
12c788f0e704: fix(auth): **signing in with Google, Facebook or GitHub no longer leaves you stuck on the consent page.** If you had signed up with a password but never clicked the verification link, then signed in with a social account using the same email, pressing **Accept** on the consent page did nothing. Signing in with the social account now counts as verifying your email, so the consent step goes through and you land in your logbook. Because that password was never confirmed as yours, it is removed, and from then on you sign in with your social account or a passkey. This also stops anyone who registered your email address with a password of their own from getting into your account.
7532a4179ba1: feat(release): **some releases now arrive with sparkles.** Now and then a release is marked as a shiny one. The first time you open We-Fly after it lands, the usual "new version" window is replaced by a holographic card floating in a night sky full of sparkles, with the same links to the release notes and the latest blog post. Move your mouse over it to watch the foil catch the light, tap the glider for an extra burst, and press **Let's fly** to send it off. Shiny releases also carry a **Shiny** tag in the changelog on the About page. If your device asks for reduced motion, the card stays shiny but nothing moves.
303bad457734: feat(airspace): **attach a competition's airspace file to your flight.** When organisers change the official airspace or add buffers for a task, open a flight's **⋯** menu and choose **Attach airspace file** to upload their OpenAir file (up to 8 MB). From then on that file is the only airspace for this flight: the map, the airspace check, the 3D replay and the Same day 3D comparison all use it, and a small **Airspace** chip next to the task shows which file it is. If another pilot already attached a file to a flight on the same task, We-Fly offers it as soon as you link the task, so nobody has to hunt for it. Files are shared with everyone and stored once, compressed. A comparison uses your own flight's file first, otherwise one of the other pilots' files.
11f3be8d64b0: feat(admin): **see how flights are spread across pilots.** The user management page can now sort users by their number of flights, and a new **Flights per User** card shows how many accounts actually fly, the median and p90 flight counts, the busiest logbook, and what share of all flights the top 10% of pilots upload.
db6b027ddcdc: feat(api): **partner apps can now download your original IGC files.** A new `GET /api/v1/flights/{id}/igc` endpoint returns the file exactly as you uploaded it, for apps you have connected with the "Read your flights" permission, and only for your own flights. Together with incremental sync and upload, this lets a flight instrument keep its logbook and your We-Fly logbook in step in both directions, without ever creating duplicates.
2d343433f1f8: feat(api): **your tasks, waypoints and routes can now sync with your flight instrument too.** Connected apps can download any task, waypoint collection or XC planner route as a `.wpt`, `.cup` or `.gpx` file, and a task exported as `.cup` carries its turnpoint radii and goal line. Your saved routes get the same two-way sync as flights, tasks and waypoints, so a route you draw in the XC planner can show up on your instrument, and one planned on the instrument lands in your planner. The "Read/Add your tasks and waypoints" permissions now say they cover routes as well.
02ccbf1559a1: feat(xc-planner): **get an XContest cloud code for routes as well as tasks, right in the briefing.** The last step of the XC planner now has an **XContest cloud code** block next to the file download and QR code. Publish your plan and you get the short code XCTrack loads with *Task → Edit → Load from XContest*, with how long it stays valid and a warning if you have edited the plan since. It works for a competition task and for a route, which XCTrack loads as a plain sequence of turnpoints. A task's code is still saved with the task; a route's code is kept only while the planner is open.
d10482e9d6df: feat(xc-planner): **see takeoffs and landings while you plan.** Two new switches under **Map layers → Points of interest** draw every known takeoff (green) and landing field (orange) on the planner map. Hover a point for its name, elevation and orientation. The layer is built to stay smooth: it loads only the part of the map you are looking at once you zoom in, draws thousands of sites in one go, and remembers what it already loaded, so panning back or switching it off and on again is instant.
d363b7a63911: feat(xc-planner): **share a public route in one click, credited to you.** Every public route in **My routes** and **Discover** now has a share button that copies its link straight to your clipboard, without loading the route first; a check mark and a "copied" message confirm it. Only saved public routes can be shared: the **Share** button stays off until your route is saved as public. Whoever opens the link sees who created the route, in the sidebar and on the map, and can save their own copy.
8d61e7e883ae: feat(xc-planner): **add notes to your saved routes and tasks.** A new notes box under the name in **Save & share** lets you write what other pilots should know: best season, conditions, landing options, safety points. Once the route or task is public, anyone who opens it from a share link or **Discover** reads your notes next to your name, in the sidebar and in the summary on the map, and the Discover lists show a one-line preview. Notes stay private while the route or task is private, and keep up to 2,000 characters.
326e82ee1966: feat(xc-planner): **shared routes and tasks now get a map preview card.** Paste the link to a public route or task in WhatsApp, Facebook, Slack or anywhere else that shows link previews, and it unfolds into a card with the route or task drawn on a small map, its name, who made it, the distance, the shape or ruleset, and the start of your notes. Tasks show every cylinder, colour-coded like in the planner, with the optimised line through them. Private routes and tasks keep the generic planner card, so nothing about them leaks through a preview.
cf5823654fc5: feat(community): **search community flights on a map.** The new **Community → Search flights** page is a big map of every takeoff the community has flown from, loaded as you move around. Click a takeoff and the traces of its community flights appear, with the list alongside (the 400 longest when a site has more), filterable by pilot or wing. Hover a trace to see who flew it, when, how far and on what wing. Click it, or a flight in the list, and its summary opens right in the side panel: times, scored distance and score, altitude, best climb, speed, thermals, ceiling and wind, with arrows to step through the other flights from that takeoff. Nothing moves on the map while you browse. When you want the whole flight, **Open the full flight in a new tab** keeps this map exactly as you left it.
50aafa31c05f: feat(community): **the pilots you follow, right on the Community page.** The **Latest flights** card now opens with a row of the pilots you follow, most recent flyer first. A ring marks those who flew this week, with their latest distance, and a tap opens that flight. Their flights in the community list carry a **Following** mark, and any other pilot there can be followed straight from the list with the **Follow** button that appears when you hover a row. Not following anyone yet? The row suggests pilots instead: people who fly your usual takeoffs, or the month's most active pilots, each with a Follow button. The list itself grew from 6 to 8 flights.
69c4fb696d1e: feat(community): **a clearer Following page.** **Community → Following** now shows the pilots you follow on the left, most recent flyer first, with a ring on anyone who flew this week. Click a pilot to see only their flights, and the link keeps that view if you share or reload it. Hover a pilot to open their profile or unfollow. On the right, their flights are grouped by day, each with a small drawing of the track, its distance, duration and max altitude. When several pilots you follow flew the same takeoff on the same day, a line says so. More flights load on their own as you scroll. A few suggested pilots sit under your list, and if you follow nobody yet, the page opens with pilots to follow instead of an empty box. On a phone, the pilots become a row of avatars above the flights.
b7e5b37dee3d: feat(takeoffs): **show only the takeoffs you can fly right now.** A new **Flyable now** switch in the takeoffs filters keeps only the sites where the current wind suits the takeoff orientation, the same check behind the green badge on each card. It works on the list, the map and your favorites, and We-Fly remembers your choice. Sites whose weather is still loading are left out until we know, and on the map the filter kicks in once you zoom in close enough to see the weather.
afe64ffe622d: feat(admin): **an email when a partner asks for API access.** Registering an OAuth application now emails the We-Fly admins with the app's details, requested permissions and a link to review it, so new requests no longer sit unnoticed in the admin panel.
7c8a6ce645ec: feat(community): **the community flights list only shows the mini map when you ask for it.** Like your logbook, the list now has a small trace icon at the start of each row. Hover it to preview the flight on a map. Moving the mouse across the rows no longer pops up a map every time, so the list is calmer to browse. On a phone, where there is no hover, each flight card has a **Preview** button that opens the map right inside the card, just like in your logbook.
412df92cf39c: chore(deps): **flight tables moved to TanStack Table v9.** Your logbook and the flights list on pilot profiles now run on the new major version of the table library. Nothing changes for you: sorting, showing or hiding columns, selecting flights for bulk edits and the trace preview work as before.
f6b3d301dc23: feat(replay): **a calmer, roomier 3D replay, the same for one flight and for the Same day comparison.** The scene now gets the space: playback sits in a solid bar under the 3D view instead of floating over it, with launch, landing, best-climb and biggest-gap markers on the timeline and speeds from 1× to 100×. All eight live values (altitude, height above ground, climb, speed, glide, wind, airspeed, time) sit in one strip at the top left, and on a phone in a grid just above the controls. The camera, a **Layers** button that shows how many layers are on, and a **More** menu (share, record a video, hide overlays, past-track length and opacity, keyboard shortcuts) share one toolbar. An airspace warning appears at the top while you are near or inside a zone, and the vario legend can be folded away. In fullscreen, the controls fade out while the replay plays and come back as soon as you move. The comparison gains a live rank beside the scene (pilot chips on a phone) with moments you can jump to, a rank strip that puts **Distance / Race** right next to the rank it changes, a charts drawer under the scene that you can resize or fold (Altitude, Phases, Circles) so no chart can squeeze the 3D view, and stats in a side panel you open from the header; on a phone, charts and stats share one sheet. Light and dark themes are both supported, and your layer choices are remembered separately for single flights and comparisons. The comparison now opens with the same drop from space as a single flight, landing on the first pilot to take off and following them until you pick someone else; in both replays the camera no longer jumps when the descent ends, and orbit zoom stops 500 m from the glider, before the ground turns to blurry pixels. The height captions over every thermal in the comparison are gone.
0b9b2eaff76e: feat(nav): **links stay inside We-Fly, and outside links say so.** Links to We-Fly pages (docs, flights, profiles, the privacy policy) now open in the same window, so the installed app on your phone no longer throws you into the browser; Back brings you to where you were. Links to other websites still open a new tab and now carry a small ↗ so it never comes as a surprise. Where leaving the page would lose your work, help now opens in a drawer instead: the **Privacy Policy** link on the upload page and **Learn more** in the date-fix window slide in over the page and leave your files and changes untouched. A new **Fixing Wrong Flight Dates** article explains when to use the date fix. Signed in, **References** and **Contact** now open inside We-Fly too, restyled like the rest of the app.
4c1f273eeabe: feat(nav): **a lighter way around We-Fly, without the left sidebar.** The top bar now holds the four places you go: **My flying** (Logbook, Cockpit, Success), **Community**, **Takeoffs** and **XC planner**, plus **Admin** for admins. A slim bar under it shows the pages of where you are, and a second row groups the rest: the ten Cockpit views, Logbook's Flights and Wings, and Community's nine pages, now sorted into **Overview, Feed, People, Stats and Challenges**. **Filters** sits at the right of that bar on the Logbook and Cockpit, with the number of active filters; your saved filters and presets are untouched. Press **⌘K** (Ctrl+K) or the magnifier to jump to any page by name. Your avatar menu now lists Profile, Shared links, Anomalies and Developer, then Documentation, What's new, About, References, Contact and Privacy policy. On a phone, five tabs sit at the bottom (Logbook, Cockpit, a big **Upload**, Community and **Me**); Me holds your notifications, Success, Takeoffs, XC planner, account pages, help and theme. Every page keeps its address, so bookmarks and shared links still work.
6d93ad7e45fb: feat(filters): **filters open in place, and search finds your flights and takeoffs.** On a computer, **Filters** now drops down a wide panel under the bar instead of covering the page: presets, flight, location, time and performance (now including a **minimum distance**) side by side, with a calendar that dots the days you flew, the matching flight count, and **Done**. Results update as you click. Each filter pill under the title opens just that filter for a quick change. On a phone, Filters is a bottom sheet with quick Season, Wing and Takeoff rows and a **Show N flights** button. The search box now sits in the top bar (**⌘K**) and finds takeoffs, your flights, pilots, pages and actions such as applying a saved preset; with nothing typed it shows your recent flights. Your saved filters and presets are unchanged. On the Logbook, the **Columns** button to show or hide table columns sits next to the Flights / Wings switch.
f76bc541f3c4: feat(nav): **a clear way back instead of breadcrumbs.** The old breadcrumb trail above pages is gone. Pages you reach from a list now start with a back link in the bar under the top menu, like a flight's **← Logbook**: a takeoff shows **← Takeoffs**, a pilot **← Pilots**, a club **← Clubs**, a season recap **← Logbook**. Signed in, the documentation now opens inside We-Fly with a quiet section menu, **← category** on each article, and Docs / What's new tabs on the home page.
c970e2333c2c: feat(xc-planner): **the XC planner and the docs join the new look.** Signed in, the XC planner now opens inside We-Fly like any other page: the three steps (Design, Airspaces, Briefing) sit in the bar under the top menu, your route settings in a panel on the left, and the distance card and **Continue** button on the map. Every planner tool is still there; Discover and route import/export now sit under **More tools**. The documentation and What's new pages get the same calm style, with the docs menu on the left and a table of contents beside each article. Takeoff pages drop the breadcrumb, since Takeoffs stays highlighted in the top bar.
d4a1fc31044a: feat(design): **every page now wears the new look.** Logbook, Cockpit and its views, Success, each flight's tabs, Community, Takeoffs, Profile, Developer and Admin share the same calm style: a clear title with a one-line summary, a row of key numbers, framed panels and quieter tables. On the Logbook and Cockpit, a filter row under the title shows each active filter as a pill you can remove, your saved presets, and how many flights match. On a flight, the tabs (Summary, 3D Replay, Phases and the rest) move up into the bar beside a back arrow to the Logbook. Nothing was taken away: every chart, table, button and setting is still there.
671723a6a8f3: feat(community): **pick flights straight from the map on your phone.** On **Community → Search flights**, tap anywhere on the traces and every flight passing under your finger shows up in a small card over the map, so overlapping traces are no longer a guessing game. Tap a pilot in the card to highlight their trace and compare, then tap **View** to open the one you want. The list below the map works the same way: a first tap highlights the trace, a second one (or **View**) opens the flight. The list is also tighter on small screens, with the distance on the right of each pilot's name, so more flights fit without scrolling. Nothing changes on a computer.
cfde1368c260: fix(api): **connected apps can no longer delete your flights.** The permission that let an app permanently remove flights from your logbook is gone, along with the endpoint behind it. Only you can delete a flight, on We-Fly. Connected apps still hear about it when you do, so their copy stays in step.
062f02691ff7: fix(contact): **contact form messages now reach the We-Fly inbox.** Messages sent from the **Contact** page go to contact@we-fly.cloud instead of a personal address, so the team can answer you from a We-Fly address. Replying still goes straight to you. The privacy policy now lists the same address for questions and data requests.
dc1b5f9e4b91: fix(community): **flight stats fit on small phones.** On the community flights list, the distance, duration, quality and route efficiency under each flight card no longer wrap or squeeze on narrow screens: they sit in two tidy rows on the smallest phones and in one spaced-out row everywhere else.
17fb450fa77e: fix(replay): **the 3D replay fits your phone.** On a phone the 3D settings now slide up as a sheet instead of covering the whole map, and the camera, share and settings buttons sit in two tidy rows. The flight 3D view and the Same day 3D comparison now offer the same settings in the same order, and the comparison gains **Vario**, **Wind profile** and **Reach** for the pilot you follow. Turning **Airspace** off in the comparison now also hides the airspace crossings in the moments list. The **Map | 3D** switch of the comparison is no longer cut off or hidden behind the close button, its tabs scroll on a phone, and the **Compare N flights** bar no longer sits on top of the bottom menu.
cc931edb1fd3: fix(nav): **you can see when there are more tabs.** Rows of tabs that don't fit the screen (a flight's tabs, Cockpit views, Admin, the pilots you follow on Community…) now fade out at the edge where more is hidden, and open scrolled to the tab you are on. Season pills on a club page no longer cover the leaderboard title on a phone.
f92e09955e72: fix(community): **map search is easier to read on a phone, and only shows real flights.** On a phone the flight details under the map now scroll normally. Flights under 5 km of XC distance are left out of the results, along with flights flagged as driving or powered, so the map shows proper flights; a link to a shorter flight still opens.
8aa3cae8a394: fix(cockpit): **the Cockpit map no longer hides behind the bottom menu on a phone.** On a phone the map is now sized to end just above the bottom menu, so you see all of it without scrolling.
3d181c84309d: fix(design): **About, the docs header and the public pages fit a phone.** The About window no longer runs off the right edge of the screen. The top menu on the docs, What's new and other public pages keeps the logo on one line and tucks its links into a menu on a phone. **References** and **Contact** wear the new look.
8a419d0db8a1: fix(flights): **flight time now counts only the time you spend in the air.** An instrument left running before takeoff or after landing kept adding that time to the flight, because GPS drift made it look like it was still moving: one flight left on overnight showed 13h30 instead of 2h30. We-Fly now finds the moment you take off and the moment you land, and drops the wait on launch, the time on the ground afterwards, and any drive to launch or back home logged in the same file (it uses the same driving detection that already spots driving-only uploads). Your duration, takeoff and landing times, track distance, score, season recap, personal bests and badges now reflect the flight itself. Flights that cross midnight UTC, typical of afternoon flights in the Americas, were also cut off at 23:59:59 and now run to their real landing. Existing flights affected by any of this are being corrected.
059452e4daf3: fix(community): **the ring around pilots you follow is no longer cut off.** Hovering a pilot in the row of people you follow on the Community page clipped the top of their avatar ring. It now shows in full, and the ring marking pilots who flew this week uses the We-Fly orange, on the Following page too.
dbdde3a76bae: fix(community): **unknown wings no longer top the recap.** Flights logged without a wing ("NKN", "Unknown (not in IGC)" and similar) were counted as a wing of their own in **Most popular wings**. They are now left out of the wing rankings and counts.
be2355364351: fix(community): **every takeoff in the recap is readable and clickable.** Long takeoff names in **Epic days** were cut off and now show in full, on phones too. Takeoff names across the recap panels now open the takeoff page.
37756a40c34b: fix(deps): **security updates.** Next.js, brace-expansion, fast-uri and DOMPurify are updated to versions that fix known vulnerabilities, including a critical one in Next.js image generation.
